notes:
Account overview: Polaris AgentWorks is a global CX platform powering enterprise retail & telco contact centers (30+ sites, 24/7). Looking to replace a hybrid stack (on-prem PBX + cloud NLU) with a unified inference substrate that guarantees predictable latency during promotions/peak season. Primary ask: dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) with VPC connectivity and option to run on-prem in European datacenters for regulated customers.

Summary of requirements: latency SLAs for agent-assist: 95th <= 350ms for short responses, p50 < 120ms; burst tolerance to 3x normal traffic for 2 hours; deterministic fallbacks to smaller quantized model if primary unavailable; tool-calling hooks to internal case system (REST + GraphQL), secure function calls through RBAC; token retention policy maximum 30 days, audit logs required.

POC notes: 2-week POC executed with Redwood Dedicated staging pool. Results: average latency p50=95ms, p95=320ms under steady 2k concurrent agent sessions. During a simulated spike (x3 concurrent), p95 increased to ~760ms for long-context summarization tasks — acceptable but legal asked for tighter guarantee. Key win: automatic KV prefix caching reduced repeated context token counts by ~40% in agent chat flows.

Stakeholder quotes: "We need absolute predictability during Black Friday windows — outages are measurable in revenue." — Head of Support Technology.

Procurement posture: procurement + legal pushing for 12–24 month committed capacity with convert-to-private option. Interested in long-term cost reduction features from Redwood Optimize (quant profiles + caching).
